modes.viewport: An independent viewport axis: type sets per viewport and a layout mode per breakpoint.

nodes.label: Levers, set by hand
nodes.purpose: Brand colors, fonts and the levers for type, shape, depth, motion and layout, set in the panels. The lever manifest describes every knob once, and both interfaces render from it.

nodes.label: design.md
nodes.purpose: A brand brief in Markdown with YAML front matter. It is a round-trip artifact: the studio exports it, and any lane can read it back in. Two dialects are read: the engine's own and the standard design.md.
inputs: Written by a person or an agent

nodes.label: Tool arguments
nodes.purpose: A brand input passed as arguments to a tool call. list_levers says what is accepted; validate_brand checks it before anything is generated.

nodes.label: Web studio
nodes.purpose: The theme studio in a browser. The engine runs in the page, so there is no backend. A person sets levers or imports a design.md, sees the result live with contrast checks per mode, and downloads tokens or a design.md.

nodes.label: Figma plugin
nodes.purpose: The same studio UI, running inside Figma. On top of everything the web studio does, it writes into the open file: variables, styles, component sets and style guides, and it keeps them current.
outputs: The brand, saved in the file

nodes.label: Agent
nodes.purpose: Any MCP client, such as Claude Code. It themes a brand from tool arguments or a design.md, scores the UI code it writes, and drives the Figma plugin by command.

nodes.label: Prism3 engine
nodes.purpose: Generates the whole token layer from the brand input: color ramps and roles, type, space, radius, shadow, motion and layout. Dependency-free TypeScript with no LLM: the same input always gives the same output.
inputs: A brand input from any lane

nodes.label: Component definitions
nodes.purpose: One TypeScript definition per component: anatomy, variants, states, token bindings, accessibility and usage prose. Figma sets, component docs and the planned coded components are projections of these.

nodes.label: DTCG tokens
nodes.purpose: W3C design tokens. Two forms: one canonical tree, and a consumer set of a base file plus one overlay per mode with no build metadata. Two producers: the engine, and TokenPress reading a Figma file.

nodes.label: Agent metadata (.ai.json)
nodes.purpose: A *.ai.json file beside each token tree: what each token means, when to use it and when not to, and which pairs it is measured against. It keeps the token files plain DTCG.
outputs: Metadata an agent reads before writing UI

nodes.label: Component docs
nodes.purpose: One Markdown page per component and one components.ai.json, both generated from the definitions. Maintainer notes stay out of both.

nodes.label: The Figma file
nodes.purpose: What the plugin, or the Figma MCP scripts, write into a file. Every item is bound to the generated variables, so a new brand repaints it.

nodes.label: Variables and styles
nodes.purpose: Figma variable collections with a mode per appearance and breakpoint, plus text, shadow, gradient and grid styles, all bound to the generated tokens.
inputs: Apply theme, from the plugin or the MCP scripts

nodes.label: Motion variables
nodes.purpose: Durations reach Figma as TIMING variables in seconds; curves, easing roles and springs as EASING variables. A transition has no Figma form, so its duration and its easing role are written instead.

nodes.label: Component sets
nodes.purpose: A component set per definition, with each family on its own page, bound to the variables. An update checks first and writes nothing, then applies after the agent confirms. Prune previews before it deletes. Labels and inverse backdrops are drawn around each set as canvas furniture, and a scrim behind the centered and bottom-sheet Dialog examples.
inputs: Component plans, through the plugin or the MCP scripts
outputs: An as-built record for safe updates

nodes.label: Style guides
nodes.purpose: Tables drawn onto the file's token pages for color, dimensions, border widths, opacity, font variables, and text, effect and gradient styles. Each specimen is bound to the variable it shows, so it repaints when a value changes. Motion, grid and breakpoint tables are specified, not built.
inputs: The plugin's Build style guides page
outputs: Pages a team reviews the brand on

nodes.label: TokenPress
nodes.purpose: A Figma plugin, in this repo and published in the Figma Community, that exports any file's variables and styles to DTCG. It runs the opposite direction from the engine and shares no code with it, so its output is an independent check.
inputs: Variables and styles in a Figma file

nodes.label: Code library
nodes.purpose: The path from tokens to coded components. The token build runs in CI today; the components and their stories are planned.

nodes.label: Style Dictionary build
nodes.purpose: A stock Style Dictionary, with no custom code, builds every brand to CSS, SCSS, JavaScript, iOS and Android in CI. It proves the tokens are consumable. No package is published yet.

nodes.label: CSS variables
nodes.purpose: CSS custom properties. Built and checked in CI; not yet shipped as a package a product can install.

nodes.label: Coded components
nodes.purpose: Web components and React components projected from the same definitions as the Figma sets, vanilla HTML and CSS first. Not built.

nodes.label: Storybook
nodes.purpose: Generated stories for each coded component. Not built.

connections.label: MCP
connections.purpose: The engine over MCP: stdio JSON-RPC, no dependencies. An agent lists levers, validates and themes a brand, themes from a brief, scores UI code, and exports files.

connections.label: Command line
connections.purpose: Compiles a design.md into tokens from the command line. Exits non-zero on a schema violation, a broken alias or a failed contrast contract. An optional fidelity report compares the brief's values with what the engine generated.

connections.label: Agent link
connections.purpose: One versioned command protocol for driving the open plugin. Commands arrive through the file's mailbox or the desktop bridge and run through the same handlers as the panel's buttons. Off by default and never persisted. In the release build nothing in a command is evaluated; the development build adds one command, run-code, for testing.

connections.label: Desktop bridge
connections.purpose: A local MCP server that relays agent link commands to the open plugin over a localhost WebSocket and streams progress back. Only the development build of the plugin may open that socket; the release build has no network access.

connections.label: Figma MCP scripts
connections.purpose: Plain Plugin API scripts for the Figma MCP's use_figma tool. They apply a theme and build components with the plugin closed, and carry the plugin's own executors, so both paths write the same file. Runs only against a designated scratch file.

checks.label: Contrast contracts
checks.purpose: Every text, icon and border role is resolved by contrast against its own surface, in every mode, and checked. A failure stops the run; a role below its floor is warned, never silent.

checks.label: Code scoring
checks.purpose: Scores UI code an agent wrote against the brand's tokens: the rate of invented tokens, primitive leaks, and contrast for the pairs it used. The score goes back to the agent.

checks.label: Token contract
checks.purpose: Names are versioned; values are not. A committed baseline lists the guaranteed token names. Removing or retyping one is a major contract change, and the baseline refuses to move until the version does.

checks.label: CI gates
checks.purpose: Every pull request regenerates every committed artifact and runs the full gate list: drift, contrast, naming, prose, builds and round trips. npm run verify runs the same list locally. Among them: the exporter agreement between TokenPress and the engine, and the Style Dictionary build.

traces.label: A designer themes a brand in Figma

steps.caption: A designer opens the plugin and sets brand colors, fonts and levers.
The engine, bundled in the plugin, generates every token and checks contrast in every mode.
Apply Theme writes the variables, then the styles bound to them.
Build turns each definition into a component set on its own page.

traces.label: A person themes a brand on the web

steps.caption: They paste a design.md on the start screen.
The engine runs in the page and rebuilds on every change, with contrast checked per mode.
Export downloads DTCG: a base file plus one overlay per mode.
The agent loads the prism3-theme skill and assembles a brand input.
It calls list_levers, then theme_brand, over MCP. The results carry the contrast checks and the decisions log.
export_theme writes the token files to a folder.
The metadata beside them says what each token is for, so the UI the agent writes uses them by name.

traces.label: An agent builds components in Figma

steps.caption: With the agent link switched on, the agent sends build-components.
The plugin runs it through the same handler as the Build button, with the engine bundled inside.
The sets are built on their own pages. Later updates check first, then apply after the agent confirms.

traces.label: Round trip through Figma and TokenPress

steps.caption: The plugin generates the tokens.
Variables and styles land in the file.
TokenPress reads them back out of the file.
Its DTCG export must match the engine's own. CI compares the two.

traces.label: A token on its way to code

steps.caption: A brand input enters the engine.
The engine writes DTCG, and every token name is checked against the contract baseline.
A stock Style Dictionary reads the files with no custom code.
It builds CSS variables, checked in CI but not yet published.
Planned: coded components bind to those variables.
Planned: stories are generated for each component.
